that he was drawn to it by Ugo Foscolo’s review of John Hookham Frere’s mock-he-
roic Prospectus and Specimen of an Intended National Work, by William and Robert
Whistlecraft, 2nd edn (1818) and William Stewart Rose, The Court of Beasts (1819), the
latter a translation of Giambattista Casti’s Animali Parlanti (1802), in Quarterly Review
xxi (April 1819) 486–556, the same number in which John Taylor Coleridge’s review of
L&C appeared. Foscolo’s learned and discerning essay, which appeared under the run-
ning head ‘Narrative and Romantic Poems of the Italians’, notices Forteguerri as ‘a writer
